turn_text: Great to be with you. Thanks for having
me. Congressman, what does the Republican Party need to do to get back to power in Washington?

I think this is actually pretty simple. I think there's a tendency to overcomplicate things, but I genuinely believe that our party and the country are in a similar situation as we were, say, in the mid-1970s. And I've often quoted as many conservatives do, remembering fondly the speech that Ronald Reagan gave to CPAC in 1975. And that was the famous time where he said, A lot of people think that we may need to pitch a third party and have some new idea, some new vision. And he rejected that. And Reagan said, this is the time for us to paint with bold colors and not speaking pale pastels. We need to present a real vision. We need to explain to the American people what it is we're for and what solutions we have to all the challenges facing the country. I think we're in a similar time. And we know the result of that ultimately. that Ronald Reagan was able to bring in a new revolution. He also said famously in his farewell address. They called me the great communicator, but I wasn't that at the end of this era. He said, I was just communicating great things. And then the same great things that had guided our nation since its founding. That's my paraphrase of his message. And so I believe that that's what should guide us today. What I mean by that is that we need to double down on the same foundational truths that our party has always stood for, our core principles. And we need to articulate those in a way that resonates with this current generation of Americans, not unlike what Reagan did in the 70s and what had been done before that. And so I define those as those core principles or things that Virtually every American does agree with, should agree with. It's the ideas of individual freedom, limited government, the rule of law, peace through strength, fiscal responsibility, free markets, human dignity, the sanctity of every single human life. Those are the things that define us not only as Republicans, but more fundamental than that as Americans. And I think if we double down on that, that's what will ensure our success.
